contexts.text: I spoke with pope Sixtus Quintus. He was chief regulator of a Catholic Society who excel the rest in judgment and industry. For half a year before his death he had believed that the vicarship was an invention for the sake of dominion; and that the Lord alone is to be adored; also that the Holy Scripture is Divine; and that the saints are not anything. He leads an active life, proposing to himself every morning nine or ten things. (He tells how he had accumulated the great treasure in the castle of St. Angelo. His message to those now living.) Compare SE 5529. SE 5833. LJPost 103.
